prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 1997 – Summary

Core vision: Build a fair, free and open society by widening opportunity, spreading power, and combining a market economy with active, accountable government. Priorities are education, cleaner environment, modernised politics, stronger communities and public services. Costed pledges accompany major proposals.

Education (flagship): Add £2bn/year funded by 1p on the basic income tax rate.
- Universal high‑quality early years for all 3–4 year‑olds (first call on funds); scrap nursery vouchers; set standards and require qualified supervision.
- Double spending on school books/equipment in year one; cut primary classes to max 30 within five years; £500m over 5 years for repairs.
- Replace National Curriculum with a Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; drive literacy; strengthen inspection (including LEAs); General Teaching Council; discipline and anti‑bullying/truancy plans.
- Devolve more power/budgets to schools; oppose selection but let local communities decide.
- Lifelong learning: individual Learning Accounts (state/employer/individual); salary‑linked loan repayment, oppose top‑up fees; credit‑based post‑14 system; link schools to the internet; 2% remissible training levy on larger firms; expand 16–19 training.

Economy and jobs:
- Independent UK Reserve Bank to keep inflation low; support joining the euro if Maastricht criteria are met and after a referendum.
- Fiscal “golden rule”; split capital/current spending; promote public‑private investment.
- Benefit transfer to turn long‑term unemployment benefits into “working benefits”; boost small business finance, abolish UBR long term; regional Development Agencies; shift R&D from military to civil.
- Tougher competition law; single utilities regulator focused on consumers; stronger consumer redress and food labelling (including GM).

Environment and transport:
- Tax shift from jobs/VAT to pollution (including phased carbon tax); national sustainability targets and annual PM report.
- National home insulation programme (targeting 2m low‑income households); energy efficiency standards; promote renewables and CHP; no new nuclear subsidies; decommissioning focus.
- Invest in public transport; enable urban road pricing; retain London Underground public ownership with access to private finance; double passengers/treble freight on rail by 2010, with sanctions on Railtrack if targets missed.
- Cleaner water, tougher shipping safety, stronger countryside protections, greener farming, product reuse/recycling push. Animal welfare: dog registration; ban cosmetics/weapon/tobacco testing; stronger transport limits; wildlife protections.

Homes, safety, communities:
- 3,000 more police within a year; restorative justice; CPS overhaul; local crime‑prevention partnerships; Royal Commission on drugs.
- Housing: more building via public/private/housing associations; release council capital receipts; Mortgage Benefit for first‑time buyers (current MIRAS retained for existing loans); end street homelessness by 2000; tackle empty/unsafe housing; fair water charging.

NHS and care:
- Extra £540m/year (from closing NI loopholes and 5p on cigarettes) for staff and prevention; halt finance‑driven closures for 6 months; unify GP funding; National Inspectorate; cut waits to max 6 months in 3 years; restore free eye/dental checks; ensure NHS dentistry access; shift from bureaucracy to care; national pay review; more nurses/doctors.
- Community care: Carer’s Benefit; national standards and charging guidance; raise asset thresholds over time.

Constitutional reform:
- Bill of Rights (ECHR into UK law); Human Rights Commission; Freedom of Information Act; reduce MPs by 200; PR for all elections; reformed largely elected second chamber; fixed 4‑year terms; party finance transparency.
- Devolution: Scottish Parliament and Welsh Senedd (PR, income tax powers); elected English regional assemblies where wanted; stronger local government, moving towards Local Income Tax; London strategic authority.
- Northern Ireland: power‑sharing, PR, civil liberties safeguards, economic co‑operation.

Opportunity and equality:
- Break poverty traps: raise tax thresholds by £200 (500k out of tax); new 50% rate over £100k; replace Income Support/Family Credit with simpler Low Income Benefit; national childcare strategy; voluntary Citizens Service; regionally variable minimum wage; crack down on fraud/evasion.
- Older people: earnings‑linked top‑up to guarantee minimum income; flexible retirement 60–70; citizenship‑based pensions; expand private/portable pensions.
- Women, disabled people, ethnic minorities, LGBT: stronger equal rights and anti‑discrimination laws; repeal Section 28; equal age of consent; independent Food Commission; fair immigration/asylum processes.

Foreign policy:
- Pro‑EU reform and enlargement; euro entry subject to criteria and referendum; CAP/CFP reform; NATO‑based defence; maintain Trident (limited warheads); UN reform, peacekeeping capacity, ICC; lead on global environment; aid rising toward 0.7% GNP in 10 years; stricter arms controls, landmine ban; fair trade with labour/environment standards.

Tax contract:
- Transparent, audited, waste‑cutting, fair. 1p basic rate rise for education; +5p on cigarettes for free checks; most taxpayers pay the same or less; excluding £100k+, average increase ~45p/week.
